rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion concerns Jews and their Sabbath transgression; the address now extends to all People of the Book, inviting belief in the confirming revelation and warning of punishment for defiance.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت الآيات السابقة - كما عرفت - متعرضة لحال اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Erasing faces and turning them backward is not annihilation: people retain their natural aims but pursue what they left behind, moving backward toward ruin.
rows.anchor: طمس الوجوه محو هذه الوجوه التي يتوجه بها البشر نحو مقاصدها الحيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people naturally seek what they regard as good, this reversal makes every pursuit yield evil, so greater effort means greater regression and no success.
rows.anchor: كلما توجه إلى ما يراه خيرا لنفسه وصلاحا لدينه أو لدنياه لم ينل إلا شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads or in its apparent disjunctive sense: the threat offers either mental reversal without changing human form, or a curse that transforms people into animals like apes.
rows.anchor: على ظاهرها من إفادة الترديد والفرق بين الوعيدين أن الأول أعني الطمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite plural faces indicates that the punishment will affect only some, not everyone; leaving their identities unspecified makes each person fear being singled out.
rows.anchor: فأتى بالجمع المنكر ولو كان المراد هو الجميع لم ينكر ولتنكير الوجوه وعدم تعيينه نكتة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rational pronoun them refers to people signified by faces, weakening the bodily-face reading and favoring reversal of their inner perception.
rows.anchor: حيث أرجع فيه ضمير " هم " الموضوع لأولي العقل إلى قوله { وجوها } كما هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is divine alteration of people’s dispositions: they turn from accepting truth and avoiding falsehood to following falsehood and avoiding truth in faith.
rows.anchor: المراد بطمس الوجوه في الآية نوع تصرف إلهي في النفوس يوجب تغيير طباعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse in this threat means metamorphosis, as in the transformation of the Sabbath violators.
rows.anchor: وكذا تبين أن المراد باللعن المذكور فيها المسخ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view takes the threat as physically turning a people’s faces toward their backs at the end of time or on Resurrection Day; al-Tabatabai rejects it because the alternative curse conflicts with that reading.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بالطمس تحويل وجوه قوم إلى أقفيتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view understands the threat as worldly humiliation and setbacks that frustrate their aims; he says this is possible but conflicts with the verse’s opening call to believe.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بالطمس الخذلان الدنيوي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported view takes the threat as expelling them from the Hijaz back to Syria and Palestine; he rejects it because the opening context supports another meaning.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد به إجلاؤهم وردهم ثانيا إلى حيث خرجوا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual turning from true religion also removes the foundations of worldly flourishing; the linked verses connect human corruption with deeds and blessings with faith and piety, allowing several proposed senses to be combined.
rows.anchor: لازم هذه الحقيقة أن طمس الوجوه عن المعارف الحقة الدينية طمس لها عن حقائق سعادة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s threatened judgment is certain and has already occurred, including curses and enmity among them lasting until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الأمر لا محالة واقع وقد وقع على ما ذكره الله

words: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, 4:48 warns of worldly consequences of shirk while 4:116 warns of its afterlife consequences, though both verses in general cover all consequences.
rows.anchor: تهدد بآثار الشرك الدنيوية وتلك آية 116 تهدد بآثاره الأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not forgive shirk because creation’s mercy rests on worship and servitude, which cannot coexist with associating partners.
rows.anchor: الخلقة إنما تثبت على ما فيها من الرحمة على أساس العبودية والربوبية

words: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sins below shirk may be forgiven through intercession by prophets, friends of God, angels, or righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: فبشفاعة من جعل له الشفاعة من الأنبياء والأولياء والملائكة والأعمال الصالحة

words: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not address repentance in this context, which concerns unbelief; repentance can bring forgiveness of every sin, including shirk.
rows.anchor: على أن التوبة يغفر معها جميع الذنوب حتى الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk here includes unbelief: even if the Quran does not label People of the Book polytheists, rejecting its confirming revelation is associating with God; rejecting Jesus after Moses is likewise rejecting God and associating Moses with Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشرك في الآية ما يعم الكفر لا محالة فإن الكافر أيضا لا يغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about associating something with God rather than naming polytheists suits the point that unbelief assigns a partner to God in His dominion.
rows.anchor: ولعل ما ذكرناه هو النكتة لقوله تعالى { أن يشرك به } دون أن يقول المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom requires that not every sinner be forgiven, or command, prohibition, and divine moral education would become pointless; some instances of every sin therefore remain unforgiven, without contradicting general promises of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: من الحكمة أن لا يغفر لكل مذنب ذنبه وإلا لغى الأمر والنهي وبطل التشريع

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives zakat from growth produced by God’s blessing.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب أصل الزكاة النمو الحاصل من بركة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes commendable self-purification by deeds from blameworthy verbal self-praise, which God forbids as ethically ugly.
rows.anchor: وتزكية الإنسان نفسه ضربان أحدهما بالفعل وهو محمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this passage’s context, those praising themselves are Jews or some of them; persistence in this vice shows they have stripped themselves of scripture’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: كان الظاهر أن هؤلاء المزكين لأنفسهم هم أهل الكتاب أو بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claims to be God’s children and beloved, to face the Fire for only a few days, and to be His chosen friends illustrate the self-praise at issue.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده ما حكاه الله تعالى عن اليهود من قولهم نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse alludes to Jews and supports the preceding account of their arrogance toward truth, refusal to believe, and divine curse as consequences of self-admiration.
rows.anchor: الآية تكني عن اليهود وفيها استشهاد لما تقدم ذكره في الآيات السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correction makes purification God’s prerogative: a person cannot treat any virtue as independently owned or rely on it as self-sufficient before God.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن تزكيتهم لأنفسهم ورد لهم فيما زكوه وبيان أن ذلك من شؤون الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-admiration is a root vice that grows into arrogance and then oppression, exploitation, and violations of people’s lives, honor, and property.
rows.anchor: وهذا الغرور والإعجاب الذي يبعث الإنسان إلى تزكية نفسه هو العجب الذي هو من أمهات الرذائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When self-exalting pride becomes a social custom, as he says it did among Jews, it endangers humanity and corrupts the earth.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا تعدى الفرد وصار خلقا اجتماعيا وسيرة قومية فهو الخطر الذي فيه هلاك النوع وفساد الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God may rightly praise or confer virtue because He owns what people possess; human self-praise claims an independence no creature has.
rows.anchor: فما كان لبشر أن يذكر لنفسه من الفضيلة ما يمدحها به سواء كان صادقا فيما يقول أو كاذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s own spoken praise of prophets exemplifies legitimate verbal purification; al-Tabatabai cites Adam, Noah, Abraham, Idris, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Jesus, Solomon, Job, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s purification is true and just, whether practical by bestowing favor or verbal by declaring someone praiseworthy; in this context it means verbal praise.
rows.anchor: أن تزكيته تعالى وإن كانت مطلقة تشمل التزكية العملية والتزكية القولية لكنها تنطبق بحسب مورد الكلام على التزكية القولية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation of fitil is the fiber in the cleft of a date stone.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد به ما يكون في شق النواة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported explanation is the material inside the date stone.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ما في بطن النواة

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
rows.claim: Reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s Household identify fitil as the dot on a date stone, naqir as its back, and qitmir as its peel; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ورد في روايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أنه النقطة التي على النواة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported meaning is dirt rolled between one’s fingers.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ما فتلته بين إصبعيك من الوسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not praise themselves; others may praise a person only for virtues God recognizes, since religion determines which qualities count as virtues.
rows.anchor: ليس لصاحب الفضل أن يعجبه فضله ويمدح نفسه بل هو مما يختص به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This teaching does not prohibit recognizing real virtue: people should honor scholars and defer to knowledge as following truth, though scholars must not boast of learning.
rows.anchor: فعلى الجاهل أن يخضع للعالم ويعرف له قدره فإنه من اتباع الحق

rows.speaker: بعض باحثينا
rows.claim: Some of the author’s fellow researchers, following Maghrebi thinkers, count reliance on oneself among human virtues.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره بعض باحثينا واتبعوا في ذلك ما ذكره المغاربة أن من الفضائل الإنسانية الاعتماد بالنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects self-reliance as a virtue and says the Quran instead teaches reliance on God and deriving strength and honor from Him.
rows.anchor: والذي يراه القرآن في ذلك هو الاعتماد بالله والتعزز بالله

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claims of being God’s children, beloved, or friends are lies, since God did not grant them those distinctions; self-purification itself attributes a partner to God’s ownership.
rows.anchor: فتزكيتهم أنفسهم ببنوة الله وحبه وولايته ونحو ذلك افتراء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm is a blameworthy act that obstructs a person from attaining good; this wording suits self-praise as a branch of shirk, following the preceding warning about shirk.
rows.anchor: وهو الفعل المذموم الذي يمنع الإنسان من نيل الخيرات ويبطئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jibt means anything without good; the author also reports that it can mean anything worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: الجبت والجبس كل ما لا خير فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported explanation makes jibt anything worshipped besides God; taghut is originally an infinitive like transgression, often used as an agent noun, and is also said to mean any being worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: وقيل وكل ما يعبد من دون الله سبحانه والطاغوت مصدر في الأصل كالطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the verse as exposing a case where some People of the Book judged the polytheists’ way better than the believers’ monotheism, thereby conceding that the polytheists believe in jibt and taghut.
rows.anchor: والآية تكشف عن وقوع واقعة قضى فيها بعض أهل الكتاب للذين كفروا على الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: أسباب النزول
rows.claim: The reported occasion of revelation says Meccan polytheists asked People of the Book to judge between their religion and the believers’ religion, and the latter judged for the polytheists; the author says a narration will follow in the report discussion.
rows.anchor: ما ورد في أسباب النزول أن مشركي مكة طلبوا من أهل الكتاب أن يحكموا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the judges people given a share of scripture intensifies the blame: learned People of the Book knew what jibt and taghut meant.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر كونهم ذوي نصيب من الكتاب ليكون أوقع في وقوع الذم واللوم عليهم

rows.speaker: ذكروا
rows.claim: A reported grammatical view takes am as detached, meaning rather, do they have any share of dominion? The question denies that they do.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن " أم " في قوله أم لهم نصيب من الملك منقطعة والمعنى بل ألهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow connected am and reconstruct the question as whether they are more entitled to prophethood or have a share of dominion; the author rejects that reconstruction because deleting the interrogative hamza is only allowed by poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: وقد جوز بعضهم أن تكون " أم " متصلة وقال إن التقدير أهم أولى بالنبوة أم لهم نصيب من الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers connected am, with the omitted alternative supplied by the preceding verse: do they possess all the authority their ruling assumes, or a share of dominion, or are they envious?
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أم متصلة وأن الشق المحذوف ما يدل عليه الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dominion includes authority over material and spiritual affairs, such as prophethood, guidance, control of people, and wealth; if they had it, their stinginess would keep them from giving even the least amount.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالملك هو السلطنة على الأمور المادية والمعنوية فيشمل ملك النبوة والولاية والهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqir is a tiny amount taken from the earth by a bird’s beak; the author compares the phrase to the preceding verse’s use of fitil for a negligible amount.
rows.anchor: النقير فعيل بمعنى المفعول وهو المقدار اليسير الذي يأخذه الطير من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that their dominion would make them withhold even a tiny amount resembles the image of people holding back the treasuries of their Lord’s mercy.
rows.anchor: ولو كان لهم ذلك لم يؤتوا الناس أقل القليل الذي لا يعتد به لبخلهم وسوء سريرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate context suggests that the envied people are the believers and the gift is prophethood, scripture, and religious knowledge.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالناس على ما يدل عليه هذا السياق هم الذين آمنوا وبما آتاهم الله من فضله هو النبوة والكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s ending says the envied people belong to Abraham’s family, so al-Tabatabai identifies them specifically as Muhammad, with the grace reaching others through him; he connects Abraham’s family with the Prophet and his household.
rows.anchor: تدل على أن الناس المحسودين هم من آل إبراهيم

words: فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies Abraham’s family as the Prophet, or the Prophet with his household, including his grandfather Ishmael and those like him.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بآل إبراهيم النبي أو هو وآله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وإسماعيل جده ومن في حذوه

words: فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet and believers are closest to Abraham means they follow him; it does not rename his followers Abraham’s family, since the verse distinguishes the followers from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم للذين اتبعوه وهذا النبي والذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great dominion includes spiritual sovereignty, especially prophethood and true authority to guide people; worldly power is not great in God’s estimation unless tied to religious virtue.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالملك ما يعم الملك المعنوي الذي منه النبوة والولاية الحقيقية على هداية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood and spiritual authority are likely included in the great dominion because the preceding list names scripture and wisdom but omits them as separate gifts.
rows.anchor: لم يعد فيما عده من الفضل في حق آل إبراهيم النبوة والولاية
